alterations.description: Dialogue: "A refugee from China....one of the three thousand new ones, they pour in everyday".
Dialogue: "I was thrown out....Blease...You'll be all right".

Dialogue: "If we were in Chungking, Mr. Elliot, third uncle would consider it unpardonable to accept. No Chinese girl would dare dine along with an American she had just met... Yen, but we're not in Chungking".
Dialogue: "He was a Nationalist general, captured and shot by the Communists".
Dialogue: "However, with a million refugees from China in Hong Kong now, and more arriving each day, it is like looking for a needle in a haystack. Why do they leave their home in China".

Dialogue: "Why, she fears, that when the Communists take over Chunking that she will be shot. She thinks they will not harm her in the house of a foreigner. Our clan has never begged for foreigner... May I see her. Third Uncle... It is full grown dark. I will send a boy to light the way... Fairy, it is I... My older Sister. I didn’t think you’d come. Of course I’d come. Now tell me what is this disgrace you have brought on our family? You accuse me? You have become a foreigner yourself. You’re free. You can return to Hong Kong... Third Uncle will not secure a passport for me... So I must stay and be shot when the Communists come. And would you stand under the protection of the foreigner and watch if your family were shot? They could flee but they will not. I am not of Chungking. I want to be free as you to live my life and forget China. If I get you a passport, will you return to the family and wipe out this obligation to the foreigner? I want only to get away. You will have your passport".
The word “former” in the sentence reading “Two men in the lift were former generals”.
Dialogue: "North Korea invaded the South. They crossed the 38th Parallel last night".

Dialogue: "So you are willing to sacrifice your country and many men for a romantic attachment to one man". "Our people are free at last. Refugees pour into Hong Kong at the rate of three thousand a day". "As men who believe in this new order, doesn’t it disturb you that so many flee from freedom?" "You are no longer Chinese. You are not facing the truth!".
